Each of the "parent" process, with <PID> from ll_sa<PID{_}, is no longer present.
Disassembly of ll_statahead_thread() code shows that all ll_sa<PID>_ thread are looping around shedule_timeout() in function epilog part waiting for the close()/release of the file to occur :
................

/*

statahead is finished, but statahead entries need to be cached, wait for file release to stop me.
*/
while (( {set_current_state(TASK_IDLE); /* matches smp_store_release() in ll_deauthorize_statahead() */ smp_load_acquire(&sai->sai_task); }
))

Unknown macro: { if (sa_has_callback(sai)) { __set_current_state(TASK_RUNNING); sa_handle_callback(sai); } else { /* Check regularly in case we have missed the wakeup */ schedule_timeout(msecs_to_jiffies(100)); } }
.................

"lustre/llite/statahead.c" 1823 lines {}66%{} 1204,0-1 68%
I have also examined the directory inodes being handled by each of the ll_sa<PID>_ and they all have their lli_opendir_key/lli_opendir_pid/lli_sa_enabled fields set to 0 and they all point point to a struct ll_statahead_info where sai_task field/pointer is populated and points to one of the present ll_sa<PID>_ task struct.
So, all of these points tend to indicate that file has been close()ed/release (and ll_deauthorize_statahead() is called) during the timing window where ll_sa<PID>_ Kthread has been created and sai_task is being initialized unprotected in start_statahead_thread().
item.summary: orphan statahead threads cause umount to hang

status.description: The issue is open and ready for the assignee to start work on it.
